newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE bunkers gain, Med ports slowly follow.
newsitem.headline: NWE bunkers gain, Med ports slowly follow.

text.p: A rally in crude prices late on Wednesday pushed up fuel oil and with it ARA and neighbouring bunker prices on Thursday, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 CST traded at around $116/$117 fob in late session, a gain of about $3 on late Wednesday. Early, sharp barge gains had led to bunker trades at $118 fob. Suppliers said early buyers bought a little too eagerly.
Enquiries in the entire ARA region amounted to about 30,000 tonnes, considered reasonable, but not unduly high by most suppliers.
"It's been a fair day today," one supplier said.

Hamburg followed ARA's lead, rising about $3 to around $123 fob. Some suppliers said they expected further price rises would be necessary, but buyers signalled their disagreement by staying out of the market.
Mediterranean prices rose on average $1 a tonne. Spanish demand was a little healthier than earlier in the week, but most ports managed only scant buying interest.
Fujairah prices were steady as Singapore ignored the overnight crude price hike, but Egyptian ports rose by about $1 a tonne. Port Said avails were very poor.
